reply.thought: The first step is to get the list of all orders to know which customers need payouts. After that, I need to verify the refunds reported by Alpha Co against the system's records before proceeding with payouts.

I have the list of orders. Now I need to check the refunds reported by Alpha Co against the actual refunds recorded for the relevant order IDs. Alpha Co reported refunds for order_ids 201 and 203, and failed on 204. I will use list_refunds() to verify the refunds.

I have listed the refunds. Alpha Co reported refunds for order_ids 201 and 203, and failed on 204. The system list shows records for 201 and 203, matching Alpha Co's successful reports. There is no discrepancy to report based on the successful refunds. Now I need to check the net balance for each customer: acme, birch, and cobalt, to determine the payout amount for each one. I will start by getting the balance for 'acme'.
The net balance for 'acme' is 54385 cents. Next, I will check the net balance for 'birch'.
The net balance for 'birch' is 40147 cents. Next, I will check the net balance for 'cobalt'.

I have successfully retrieved the net balances for all customers: acme (54385), birch (40147), and cobalt (33079). I have also verified the refunds and confirmed no discrepancies to warrant a hold. Now I must record a payout for each customer. I will start with 'acme'.
Payout recorded for 'acme'. Next, I will record the payout for 'birch'.
Payout recorded for 'birch'. Finally, I will record the payout for 'cobalt'.
All payouts have been successfully recorded for acme, birch, and cobalt. I can now complete the task by reporting the payouts.
